claim: One click opens a running four-player sample.
sandbox: fresh browser context; enter from the first-screen action and directly through both /demo and ?demo=1

claim: The demo never reads or changes a real game.
sandbox: save named real data, enter and change the demo, exit, then assert the real data is unchanged and demo storage is empty

claim: Reset demo restores the original sample.
sandbox: advance the demo, reset it, then assert Priya is active on turn three with the seeded history

claim: Start for real discards demo data.
sandbox: change the demo, choose Start for real, then assert the demo database is empty

claim: After the first visit, the demo works without a connection.
where: landing facts and install note, offline page, manifest, README, llms.txt
sandbox: fresh /demo context; obtain service-worker control, set offline, reload, and complete a turn

claim: The timer supports two to eight players.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; start valid two-player and eight-player clocks while asserting the controls reject one and nine

claim: Tableclock is free to use.
sandbox: fresh demo; complete a turn and assert there is no account, subscription, or payment gate

claim: Player names, preferences, and an unfinished clock stay in this browser.
where: landing facts, privacy page, README, llms.txt
sandbox: fresh real namespace; save a named bank game, close the page, reopen it, and inspect tableclock-local

claim: The app sends no player names, clock settings, or activity to a server.
sandbox: capture every request during complete demo and real turn flows; assert GET-only static requests with no XHR, fetch, or cross-origin traffic

claim: Tableclock does not use accounts.
sandbox: complete a demo interaction, open privacy, and assert no account gate or account controls

claim: Tableclock does not use analytics.
sandbox: capture the complete demo and privacy flow, then assert no XHR or fetch analytics traffic

claim: A setup link restores every player name and clock rule.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; create a link, open it on a second page, and assert all four names and every rule

claim: A setup link does not upload its player names or clock rules.
sandbox: create and open a fragment-based demo setup link while asserting no request URL or body carries the payload

claim: Count up tracks time used.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; select Count up, start, and assert elapsed time increases

claim: Time bank gives each player one decreasing budget.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; start a five-second Time bank and assert the active bank decreases

claim: Bank with increment returns the chosen increment after a turn.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; start five seconds with a three-second increment, end a turn, and assert the returned time

claim: Per-turn limit gives the next player a fresh limit.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; spend part of a five-second turn, advance, and assert the next player receives about five seconds

claim: Arrow keys reorder players, retain focus, and match the move buttons.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; use Arrow Up, assert order and focus, then use the matching move button

claim: Tab moves to the next setup control without a trap.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; tab through every tabbable setup control in visible order, then assert Tab leaves setup for the footer without a trap

claim: Export setup downloads the current player names and clock rules.
sandbox: fresh demo; download the setup and parse its names and timing settings

claim: Import a setup restores valid player names and clock rules.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; import a valid setup file and assert its names, mode, and duration

claim: Tableclock runs on one shared phone.
where: landing facts, illustration, running clock, terms, README
sandbox: fresh demo setup; assert the visible one-device statement and absence of room or sync actions

claim: Tableclock does not track scores.
sandbox: fresh demo setup; assert the visible limitation and absence of score controls

claim: Tableclock does not connect or sync phones.
where: landing facts and limitations, running clock, privacy, terms, README
sandbox: fresh demo setup and running clock; assert the limitation and absence of room or sync actions

claim: Tapping the active field starts the next player’s turn.
sandbox: fresh running demo on turn three; tap Priya's active field and assert Sora begins turn four

claim: Pause stops the active clock, and Start resumes it.
sandbox: fresh running demo; pause, assert the display stays fixed, resume, and assert it changes

claim: Reverse changes the direction of the next turn.
sandbox: fresh running demo on Priya; reverse direction and assert Lionel follows

claim: Mark out skips a player until Bring back restores them.
sandbox: fresh running demo; mark Sora out, assert the turn skips her, then bring her back

claim: Sound cues are short tones made on this device.
sandbox: fresh running demo with an instrumented Web Audio API; end a turn and assert a local oscillator starts with no data request

claim: A pointer tap can vibrate the device at a turn change when vibration is enabled.
sandbox: fresh running demo with an instrumented Vibration API; tap the active field and assert the turn pattern

claim: Tableclock can be installed from the site.
sandbox: fresh demo; validate the standalone manifest, maskable icon, registered service worker, and controlled reload
